sentences.text: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SURESHWAR THAKUR
HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE SUDEEPTI SHARMA

Present: Mr. Sushil Jain, Advocate for the petitioners.
 Mr. Ankur Mittal, Addl. A.G. Haryana with  Mr. Saurabh Mago, DAG, Haryana.

** *
SURESHWAR THAKUR, J. (ORAL)

1. The petitioners' lands were subjected to acquisition through Notification No.20 dated 06.02.1976 (Annexure P-2), becoming issued under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter in short referred to as "the Act of 1894").
The said Annexure became succeeded by a declaration made on 12.01.1977 (Annexure P-3), under Section 6 of the Act of 1894.
Subsequently, in pursuances thereof, an Award dated 15.04.1978, became rendered by the Collector concerned.

Even after the said acquisition proceedings becoming terminated way back in the year 1978, yet the petitioners have made a challenge to the said launched acquisition proceedings, thus on the premise that they are entitled to be bestowed, with the benefit of the provisions of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013(hereinafter in short referred to as "the Act of 2013") 1 of 4 Neutral Citation Asa Ram And Ors vs State Of Haryana And Anr on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51646311/

sentences.text:
Moreover, the further ground, as taken to make a challenge to the launching of the said acquisition proceedings, besides, for the disputed lands becoming released from acquisition, is grooved in the factum that, the acquired lands, became so acquired for a specific public purpose,
inasmuch as, for construction of a road thereons, but since the road, for which the acquired lands became so acquired, has not been constructed thereons.
3.
Consequently, it is prayed that the public purpose, for which the acquired lands became subjected to acquisition, does no longer survive, thereby, the acquired lands be released from acquisition.

4. Insofar as, the prime ground raised in the instant writ petition relating to the present petitioners becoming bestowed with the benefit of Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013, is concerned, the said ground is not available to be recoursed by the present petitioners.

The reason being that a perusal of the reply on affidavit, furnished to the instant writ petition, besides a perusal of the averments made in the writ petition, do make candid speakings, that not only Rapat possession became assumed over the acquired lands in the year 1977, but also mutation of ownership became attested in favour of the beneficiary department concerned, vide Mutation bearing No.1829 dated 16.04.1980 (Annexure R-1).
5.

Since apart from that, the compensation amount has been stated in the reply and affidavit, to not only become deposited, in terms of Section 31 of the Act of 1894, but also amongst 47 co-owners in the disputed lands, 27 successfully claiming the releases of said deposited compensation amounts.

6. In the wake of the above, the remaining co-owners in the acquired lands of the petitioners, thus,
cannot at this belated stage claim release of the acquired lands, especially when the acquisition proceedings 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:162510-DB CWP-17937-2016 [N.C.
No.2023:PHHC:162510-DB] became concluded in the year 1977, and the instant writ petition has been filed much belatedly therefrom, thus, in the year 2016, thereupon, but on the ground of delay and laches, the instant petition is a misconstituted petition.
7.

Moreover, in the wake of the said withdrawals of compensation being made by 27 co-owners, out of the 46 co-owners concerned, thereby, too the instant petition is barred by the principle of estoppel arising from abandonments and waivers, as till lawful partition of joint lands takes place,
thereupto, the principle of unity of title and community of possession inhering in the joint landowners, thus, survives.
Resultantly, no specific portion of the acquired lands can be exclusively claimed by the present petitioners.

8. Though, the learned counsel for the petitioners vehemently argues that the public purpose, for which the acquired lands, became subjected to the acquisition proceedings, inasmuch as, for construction of the road, rather has not been fructified, inasmuch as, the said public road has not been constructed on the acquired lands.
Therefore, he submits that, thereby the acquired lands are required to be released from acquisition.

sentences.text:
However, the above made contention is not accepted by this Court, as on a reading of the reply on affidavit furnished to, the writ petition, it is revealed that, as a matter of fact, out of the total acquired lands, the road could not be completed or constructed, but only upon an area measuring 06 kanals, 15 marlas, rather given the land-losers concerned making encroachments thereons.
10. The makings of the said encroachments or trespassings, upon the acquired lands by the co-owners concerned, but after complete vestment of right, title and interest, thus, in the beneficiary department, which thus occurs immediately, on the issuance of a notification under Section 4 of the Act of 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:162510-DB CWP-17937-2016 [N.C.
No.2023:PHHC:162510-DB] 1894, when is evidently working as an impediment or as an obstacle for the completion of the road, on the said minimal fragmentary portion of the acquired lands.

Therefore, the assumption of possession thereovers, yet by the land-losers concerned, is naturally,
as above-stated, but as trespassers thereons.
11. Moreover, they are evidently impeding the completion of the road for which the acquired lands became acquired.

In consequence, the present petitioners are directed to forthwith deliver vacant free possession of the said minimal fragmentary portion of land measuring 06 kanal 15 marlas, to the beneficiary department,

so that thereby the road for which the acquired lands, became acquired,
as such, becomes completed at the site concerned.
12. With the afore observations, the instant petition stands disposed of.
(SURESHWAR THAKUR) JUDGE (SUDEEPTI SHARMA) JUDGE December 18, 2023
